Spring Break Transportation Arizona: College, Family & Party Guide

Arizona is a premier spring break destination every March. Warm, sunny weather, legendary resort pools, the Grand Canyon and Sedona within a day trip, Cactus League baseball and Scottsdale nightlife pull in college groups, families, bachelor parties and couples. Here is how to move all of them, with the vehicles and rates we actually book.

Why Spring Break in Arizona?

  • Weather: 75 to 85°F and sunny
  • Pools: Resort day clubs that are events in themselves
  • Nightlife: Old Town Scottsdale clubs among the best in the West
  • Day trips: Grand Canyon, Sedona and the desert
  • Baseball: Cactus League spring training
  • Golf: Peak season, perfect conditions

Transportation by Spring Break Type

The College Crew

Reality: Big groups, multiple stops a day, a nightlife-heavy schedule, tight budgets and real safety concerns.

Our solution: The Party Bus (28 Pax) for 15 to 28 friends is one cost split many ways, a pre-party on wheels, venue-to-venue service and safe late-night returns. A 6-hour nightlife tour is $1,500 before tax ($1,620 with tax): $75 per person with 20 aboard, about $54 with all 28. For 10 to 14, the Executive Sprinter does the same 6 hours for $870 before tax ($940 with tax), $87 per person with 10 aboard or about $62 with 14.

The Family Vacation

Reality: Several generations, kid-friendly timing, lots of day trips, early nights and car seats.

Our solution: The Luxury SUV for families of up to 6 handles car seats, all ages and day trips. An 8-hour day bills 7 hours for $875 before tax, $945 with tax. Luggage and gear fit confirmed separately. Extended families take the Executive Sprinter: multiple car seats, comfortable grandparents, room for gear.

The Bachelor or Bachelorette Party

Reality: Celebration first, multiple venues a night, pool parties into nightclubs, surprises and photos.

Our solution: The Party Bus (28 Pax) is the spring break celebration vehicle. An all-day-into-night 10-hour booking bills 9 hours for $2,250 before tax, $2,430 with tax. Twenty guests pay about $113 each; 25 pay $90 each. For a crowd larger than 28, the 56-Passenger Motorcoach runs $325/hr on a 5-hour minimum; 6 hours is $1,950 before tax, about $35 per person with 56 aboard.

The Couple's Escape

Reality: Romance, upscale preferences, flexible days, dinners out.

Our solution: The Luxury SUV, airport to resort ($225 one-way, before tax), dinner transfers and day trips in comfort. A transfer is flat within 15 road miles from pickup to drop-off; longer transfers are priced from the drive with the empty return included.

Drinking on Board

For the adults: yes, you can drink on board. Arizona's open-container law, A.R.S. § 4-251, exempts passengers in a vehicle for hire such as a party bus or limousine. It is BYOB, everyone drinking must be 21 or older, and the driver never drinks. This matters for college groups: if anyone on board is under 21, there is no alcohol on the vehicle at all. Spring Break Activities

Pool Party Transportation

Resort day clubs at the W Scottsdale, Sanctuary on Camelback, the Fairmont Princess and Talking Stick Resort. We drop at the resort, pick up when you text and keep the evening going.

Nightlife Tours

Scottsdale's hot spots cluster on and around Scottsdale Road. Pre-party transportation, venue hopping, late-night stamina and a safe ride home every time.

Day Trip Adventures

The Grand Canyon, Sedona and the Verde Valley, desert hikes at Camelback or Pinnacle Peak and horseback rides. A 10-hour day trip in the Executive Sprinter bills 9 hours: $1,305 plus 8% tax, about $93 per person with 14 aboard.

Spring Training Baseball

Fifteen MLB teams across ten stadiums. Stadium drop-off, multi-game days, tailgate capability and post-game dinner. See the spring training experience page.

Sample Spring Break Itineraries

The Epic Week (College Group)

  • Day 1: Airport pickup for the whole crew, resort check-in, pool afternoon, dinner in Old Town
  • Day 2: Pool day, then a full Scottsdale nightlife tour
  • Day 3: Sedona or Grand Canyon day trip, easy evening
  • Day 4: Spring training game, post-game dinner, big night out
  • Day 5: Late start, desert adventure or spa, final night
  • Day 6: Pool morning, airport transportation

The Family Adventure Week

  • Days 1 and 2: Resort and pool
  • Day 3: Grand Canyon day trip
  • Day 4: Sedona
  • Day 5: Spring training game
  • Day 6: Phoenix Zoo and museums
  • Day 7: Departure

Each day is its own hourly booking, so you only pay for the days you need a vehicle.

Spring Break Tips

Booking Advice and Cancellation

Availability varies by date and by vehicle. Request a current quote for your date and we will confirm what is open.

Cancellation terms depend on your date and booking; read the cancellation policy before you book. One free date change when you ask 72 or more hours ahead. Full details at /policies.

Safety First

Spring break celebrations and DUI enforcement go together in Arizona. A professional, licensed chauffeur removes the risk entirely. Judgment-free service, safety first, fun facilitated responsibly.

Local Tips

Clubs charge cover and enforce dress codes; arrive before 11 PM for easier entry, and bottle service is worth a look for groups. Sunscreen is essential even when the dry heat fools you, and evenings can drop into the 50s, so bring a layer.
